14. Learned Advocate further submits that there are four packets of objectionable goods seized, but there was no identification or specification or evidence that from which packet these 5 Grams of white powder were taken and sent for chemical examination. Had it been a case that from each packet white powder was taken separately and the same were examined by the chemical examiner separately and separate reports were given in respect of each and every packet, there might be a presumption that each packet contained white powder mixed with heroin, but there was no examination of white powder from each packet on the above basis and the record shows only 6.5 Grams of white powder were received by the Chemical examiner without identifying the packets. Learned Advocate submits that it might be that from only one packet 5 Grams of white powder were taken and not from other packets. Such a circumstances gives a clear presumption that there might be some elements of heroin in one packet, but not in other three packets. So, he submits that all these things together create a bona fide and strong doubt to the effect that the prosecution failed to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubts as regards ascertainment of quantity of heroin in the four packets. We find substance in the above contentions of Mr. Mostafa. 

 25. Although the prosecution failed to prove heroin above 25 grams in this case, yet it will not call for a total exoneration from the charge of carrying heroin inasmuch as it has been proved that she carried some element of heroin mixed with powder, and, as such, it will lead to a presumption that she carried heroin below 25 grams. So, she cannot be absolved from the charge under Clause 1(a) of the Table of section 19(1) of the Narcotics Control Act, which carries sentence ranging from two years to ten years rigorous imprisonment.
